Before style truly natures,
there must be a fundamental and
sympathetic design theme in all
elements that are used together


Decorators enthusiastic about
the modern style first took their
cue from the modern architect
and talked about plans"


Backgrounds were predomin-
antly in the neutral colors of
gray, beige, white. These SEEM
ingly spacious rooms contrasted
advantageously with the rooms
decorated in the traditional style,
where floral designed wallpaper
and floor covering made a room
seem busy, cluttered and con-
fused.


Reaction Sets In.


But the pendulum swung too
far. Designers of all home fur
nishings carried the idea of SIM
plicity so far that plainness and
starkness resulted.


Rooms become stiff, sterile and
laboratory-like. Then decorators
discovered color and texture.
Modern furniture at last had the
soft and warm background its
simple lines required.


The consumer was caught in
the conflict between the decora-
tor and the architect who didn't
believe in using color. But the
aesthetic demands of many were
still not satisfied.


Instinctively. man has always
used design motifs in his living
quarters even when he knew only
crude comforts. At first, the de-
sign motifs were traditional. But
for some reason the designers in
fabrics, wallpapers and floor COW
ering never seemed to meet all
critical standards. Evidently the
designers tried too hard to be new
or different.


Primitive Inspiration.


Since the war, a change has
taken place. Materials with ap-
piled design are now available
that fit perfectly with the modern
schemes. On the premise that
pure design was a natural attri-
butte of primitive man and that
the true aim of the contemporary
designer was to recapture that
basic clarity of line, form and
proportion, one modern designer
draws upon primitive sources for
inspiration.


The designers work is hand
screened on both fabric and wall
paper. Generously, two hues
closely balanced in value are used
in combinations.


When you see these designs
with the best modern furniture,
you know the designers are doing
a good job.

NEW YORK, July 5.-A non
scheduled airline and the Civil
Aeronautics Board each blamed
the other today for the plight of
220 students and teachers strand
ed here after the CAB refused to
clear four flights to Europe.


The airline accused the CAB of
arbitrary action to eliminate COM
petition with major airlines.


The CAB in turn blamed Over
seas National Airways for failing
to meet a clearance deadline and
failing to convince the CAB that
its flight met regulations.
Safety Not Involved.


Safety was not involved, how
ever, and the CAB said the COM
pany would be cleared for overseas
flying, even if the student flights
were banned.


Meanwhile. a party of 65 college
students and teachers about to
take off for Europe were bumped"
yesterday and told their plane
had been requisitioned for a Pa

The travellers had arranged
their trip through Youth Argosy,
Inc. of Northfield, Mass. The line
involved was Seaboard 81 Western
Airlines. Inc. which handles
Youth Argosy trips. Wallace Meth,
traffic manager for the airline,
said:


1--WE had already sent a couple
Of Douglas DC-4s to the Pacific
airlift and when more equipment
was requested we found we had
to postpone our Youth Argosy
trips and reschedule them a few
days later"


Other Lines Get Requests.

Air Force had asked other airlines
to provide airlift equipment.


The group of 220 stranded here
were to leave in four flights at
various times over the week end.


Their trip was sponsored by the
All Nations Institute. Inc, and
International Youth, Inc, both
international educational travel
groups.

telegram to President Truman,
asking his assistance in the same
fashion as $50 students who were
stranded here when the Coast
Guard declared their Norwegian
cruise ship unsafe. The President

The Senate will move over the
weekend from its historic chamber
to the old Supreme Court room in

reconstruction job.

preparations this morning for the
transfer.


= Final approval of the move was
reached late yesterday when the
Senate adopted a resolution Off
cially ordering the transfer. This
followed recommendation for the

cratic Policy Committee.


The reconstruction is to con-
tinue the work which last summer
replaced the old Senate roof with
a new one and reconditioned the
chamber walls down to the gal
lery.


The work expected to consume
the rest of this year will include
tearing out the old galleries, re-
placing them with steel and fire.
proof construction and installa-
ton of new seats. The Senators

still has not decided what to
